channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: O novo balanço do STF sobre os condenados por participação em atos golpistas
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes released a report showing that 1,402 defendants have been held responsible for the January 8, 2023, coup attempts, representing 75% of the 1,878 individuals denounced by the Prosecutor General's Office. Additionally, 552 cases were resolved through non-prosecution agreements, and 169 definitive prison sentences have been issued, including 55 under house arrest and 111 in closed regime, with penalties reaching up to 27 years and three months.

item.title: Girão critica atuação da PF e aponta restrições à liberdade de expressão
item.description: Senator Eduardo Girão (Novo-CE) criticized the Federal Police for ordering a citizen to remove a banner reading 'thief' displayed from his apartment balcony during President Lula's agenda in Presidente Prudente (SP). He called the action censorship and a violation of constitutional free speech protections under Articles 5, 220, and 53. Girão also accused the STF of intimidating legislators and claimed a dictatorial regime is emerging.

item.title: Aliados de Haddad minimizam Quaest e apostam que petista ainda pode alcançar Tarcísio
item.description: Allies of Fernando Haddad downplay the Quaest poll showing Tarcísio de Freitas ahead in voter intention for São Paulo governor, saying there is room to narrow the gap as the pre-campaign advances in the countryside. They highlight the rise in Tarcísio’s rejection rate to 54% as a sign of opportunity. Currently, Tarcísio leads with 36% in the first round and 49% in the second, compared to Haddad’s 26% and 28%.

item.title: Líder do PL abraça Messias durante sabatina e diz que foi por ‘educação’
item.description: PL Chamber leader Deputy Sóstenes Cavalcante (RJ) defended his embrace of Attorney General Jorge Messias during the CCJ hearing as a gesture of courtesy, not political endorsement. Despite the cordial interaction, PL senators will vote against Messias’ STF nomination by President Lula due to partisan opposition. Messias, Lula’s nominee, requires 14 votes in the CCJ and 41 in the plenary for approval, amid political tension between the government and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre.

item.title: Roberto Jefferson volta a dizer a Moraes que não tem condições de pagar multa
item.description: Roberto Jefferson's defense reiterated to Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes that the former deputy cannot afford the R$972,600 fine imposed by the Court, calling it confiscatory. If annulment is not possible, they request a reduction and payment in installments of up to one minimum wage. Prosecutor General Paulo Gonet opposed annulment but suggested installment payments as a condition for granting semi-open regime.

item.title: Governo vê ação de Alcolumbre contra Messias e teme derrota inédita no Senado
item.description: Lula’s government allies fear that a maneuver by Senator Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP) could block Jorge Messias’s nomination to the Federal Supreme Court, currently under review in the Senate’s Constitution and Justice Committee. While Messias undergoes questioning, Lula’s allies requested an emergency meeting with the Senate president to prevent an unprecedented defeat in the nomination process.

item.title: Elogio de Messias a Flávio, linha direta com Planalto, clima de apreensão e silêncio de Alcolumbre: os bastidores da sabatina por vaga no STF
item.description: The sabatina of Jorge Messias for a seat on the Supreme Federal Court (STF) in the Senate was marked by apprehension and uncertainty about the vote outcome, with senators speculating on the silence of Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, who allegedly distanced himself from the Planalto after the nomination and is, according to allies, working against Messias’ approval. Despite this, government leader Jaques Wagner suggests that Alcolumbre’s opposition may be a positive sign, indicating Messias is likely to win, as he needs at least 41 votes and estimates range from 42 to 49 in favor.

item.title: Zema critica Messias e ironiza proximidade de Lula com indicados ao STF
item.description: Former governor Romeu Zema criticized Lula's Supreme Court appointments, alleging favoritism and lack of technical criteria, and proposed that nominees be pre-screened by the STJ, OAB, CNJ, and MP before final presidential selection. He ironically remarked that Lula could have appointed relatives, given that he already named his personal lawyer and PT allies. Zema argued that judicial appointments should not be discretionary acts of the presidency but an institutional process to safeguard the Court's independence.

item.title: Seif questiona Messias sobre parecer para atuação institucional de Janja
item.description: Senator Jorge Seif (PL-SC) questioned Attorney General Jorge Messias about the AGU's institutional opinion regarding the official activities of First Lady Janja da Silva in national and international events. Seif cited Normative Orientation No. 94, dated April 4 and signed by Messias, to demand clarification on the legal limits of Janja's institutional role.

item.title: Leia a tese de Messias que causou controvérsia em sabatina
item.description: The doctoral thesis of Jorge Messias, Attorney General of the Union and nominee to the Supreme Federal Court, criticizes Operation Lava Jato as superficial and irresponsible, accusing it of criminalizing politics and state action, and labels the impeachment of Dilma Rousseff as a coup. The work also highlights Lula’s environmental policy as central to his government, contrasting it with previous administrations, and notes a radicalized opposition since 2023 that hinders his third term.

item.title: ‘Sempre foi Deus’: Messias usa pulseira com frase religiosa em sabatina no Senado
item.description: Union Attorney General Jorge Messias wore a bracelet reading 'always was God' during his Senate hearing for a Supreme Court vacancy, drawing attention for its religious symbolism. He stressed that his evangelical faith does not influence his institutional duties, advocating for a clear but collaborative secular state that fosters dialogue with all religions without favoritism. Messias affirmed he would uphold the Constitution without religious bias, despite support from evangelical leaders for his nomination.

item.title: Crédito para motoristas será anunciado separado do novo Desenrola, diz ministro do Trabalho
item.description: Labor Minister Luiz Marinho announced that credit for drivers will be released separately from the new phase of the Desenrola program, which focuses on debt renegotiation and is set to launch next Monday. The government will split the package into two stages: first, addressing indebtedness using FGTS funds (up to 20% of balance for workers earning up to five minimum wages), and second, stimulating credit for investment, including specific lines for taxi drivers, truckers, and other categories. President Lula is expected to preview the program in a Workers' Day broadcast, with restrictions on online gambling use to prevent renewed indebtedness.

item.title: Sóstenes se justifica após repercussão de abraço em Messias
item.description: Federal deputy Sóstenes Cavalcante (PL-RJ) defended his embrace of Attorney General Jorge Messias during the CCJ Senate hearing, stating it was a courteous gesture and not a political endorsement of Messias’s STF nomination. He emphasized that the Liberal Party has already decided to oppose the nomination, with all its senators set to vote against it. The incident followed backlash from allies and social media users who interpreted the hug as support.

item.title: Líder do PL abraça Messias em sabatina, é criticado e se explica: 'Princípio de educação'
item.description: The leader of the PL in the Chamber of Deputies, Sóstenes Cavalcante, embraced Attorney General Jorge Messias during a Senate hearing, drawing criticism from Bolsonaro supporters. He defended the gesture as a 'principle of education' and denied political endorsement, emphasizing that the PL bloc will vote against Messias’ Supreme Court nomination.

item.title: Aldo Rebelo sugere 'emendão' para destravar obras e faz crítica ao STF: 'O Brasil é um país interditado'
item.description: Presidential pre-candidate Aldo Rebelo (DC) criticized the Supreme Federal Court (STF) and other institutions for blocking infrastructure projects in Brazil, advocating for a constitutional 'emendão' to streamline investments. He argued Brazil is not poor but 'interdicted' by institutional barriers, citing the stalled Ferrogão railway as an example. Rebelo proposed legal and constitutional reforms to limit the power of entities like the Federal Prosecutor's Office, Ibama, Funai, and lower courts to halt projects.

item.title: Moraes cita ataques à "independência dos juízes" ao defender continuidade de inquérito das fake news
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes defended the continuation of the fake news inquiry, stating that mass disinformation has become the primary weapon attacking judicial independence and democratic elections in Brazil. He emphasized that the investigation uncovered a criminal structure involving threats against justices, leaks of confidential data, funding of digital campaigns, and an attempted coup, including an explosion attempt at the Court’s headquarters. The report linked these acts to the January 8 events and efforts to delegitimize the Judiciary and the electoral system.

item.title: Saque do FGTS será ‘carimbado’ para pagamento de dívidas e governo deve liberar R$ 4,5 bilhões, diz ministro do Trabalho
item.description: The federal government is preparing a new phase of the Desenrola program, allowing workers earning up to five minimum wages to use up to 20% of their FGTS balance to pay off high-interest debts, such as credit card and overdraft balances. Funds will be transferred directly to creditors, bypassing the worker’s account, and participants will be temporarily barred from online gambling. The initiative aims to release R$ 4.5 billion, potentially up to R$ 8 billion, with launch expected next Monday and further details to be provided by the Ministry of Finance.

item.title: Messias defende advocacia durante sabatina ao STF
item.description: Union Attorney General Jorge Messias defended the legal profession during his STF confirmation hearing, rejecting the claim that the Court had become a 'lawyer’s bench'. He argued the STF must return to judicial magistracy, except for Minister Fux, and stressed judicial independence. His remarks came in response to Senator Carlos Portinho.

item.title: Sabatina: A opinião de Messias sobre anistia, uma obsessão bolsonarista
item.description: Jorge Messias, Lula's nominee to the Supreme Federal Court, stated during his Senate CCJ hearing that legislative authority, not executive or judicial, holds competence over amnesty matters. He argued Congress is the proper forum for high-voltage social debates, though he did not directly address Bolsonarist calls for amnesty for those involved in the coup attempt. STF ministers, including Alexandre de Moraes, have previously rejected legislative pardon for crimes against democracy.

item.title: Messias diz que 'voto popular é princípio' caro ao ser questionado sobre eleição para o mandato-tampão ao governo do Rio
item.description: The head of the Union's General Counsel, Jorge Messias, stated during his Senate hearing that 'popular vote is a very dear principle' when commenting on the election for the interim governorship of Rio de Janeiro. He declared himself 'totally against abortion' and received government backing for his STF nomination, despite Senate leadership opposition. His confirmation vote is secret and expected to be tight, with around 45 favorable votes projected.

item.title: Cortejado por Flávio e repelido por Nikolas, quem é Cleitinho, líder das pesquisas em MG
item.description: Cleitinho Azevedo, Republican senator and current leader in Minas Gerais gubernatorial polls, remains undecided five months before the first round on whether to continue his candidacy or support Governor Mateus Simões’ (PSD) reelection. His 'outsider' stance within Brazil’s center-right — opposing Lula but rejecting Bolsonaro loyalism, notably criticizing the 6×1 work scale and military pensions — has fueled doubts about his governance capacity. This choice will significantly influence the 2026 presidential race.

item.title: ‘Sou de direita… mas não posso viver de lacração’, diz Celina Leão
item.description: District of Federal Governor Celina Leão (PP) said she is on the right but believes dialogue is what will bring benefits to the population. She justified her request for a meeting with President Lula as an effort to ease the financial deterioration of the Bank of Brasília (BRB), rejecting polarization and 'lacração' rhetoric.

item.title: Senadores dizem ter recebido pedido de Alcolumbre para votar contra Messias
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (Union Party-AP) reportedly asked at least two senators to vote against the nomination of Jorge Messias to the Supreme Federal Court (STF), according to sources speaking to Folha de S.Paulo. The request emerged during the confirmation process, raising concerns about political interference in judicial appointments.

item.title: Encontro no TSE debate inclusão e acessibilidade no processo eleitoral
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) hosted the event 'Electoral Justice for All - Together for Accessibility and Inclusion' to strengthen political participation of people with disabilities. The event featured singer Sara Bentes, known as the voice of the electronic voting machine synthesizer (Letícia), who emphasized the importance of autonomous and dignified voting for people with visual impairments or low vision.

item.title: Senado decide sobre Messias, candidato de Lula ao STF
item.description: The Senate will decide on Wednesday (29) whether to confirm or reject President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's nomination of Messias to the Supreme Federal Court (STF). The vote takes place amid heightened political tensions just months before the 2026 elections, with the STF at the center of debates over judicial independence and partisan influence.

item.title: Por que a Avenida Paulista será palco da extrema-direita no Dia do Trabalhador
item.description: São Paulo's Military Police denied CSP-Conlutas permission to hold its May 1st labor demonstration on Avenida Paulista, citing the chronological order of permit applications, as the right-wing group 'Patriotas do QG' had submitted its request in September 2024, while the union filed in March 2025. CSP-Conlutas relocated its event to Praça da República and condemned the decision as arbitrary and an attack on workers' right to protest. The Paulista gathering will be led by real estate agent Carlos Silva, a supporter of Flávio Bolsonaro, with backing from groups affiliated with the União Brasil Project.

item.title: Zema defende que indicação de ministros ao STF se dê por listra tríplice de STJ, OAB, CNJ, OAB e MP
item.description: Romeu Zema, presidential pre-candidate from Novo, advocated for a triple list system to select STF ministers, involving STJ, CNJ, OAB, and MPF, to reduce political influence in appointments. He also reiterated prior proposals, including a minimum age of 60 and 15-year terms for STF justices, and expressed confidence in the future impeachment of ministers involved in controversies.

item.title: Messias diz que ‘ninguém pode ser investigado a vida toda’ após ser questionado sobre o inquérito das fake news
item.description: Jorge Messias, nominee to the Supreme Federal Court and current Attorney General of the Union, stated during his Senate hearing that investigations cannot continue indefinitely, emphasizing that criminal proceedings must have a 'beginning, middle, end, and reasonable timeframe'. He avoided commenting directly on the fake news inquiry, citing future judicial responsibilities, but stressed his commitment to constitutional principles such as reasonable duration of process, natural judge, and proportionality, which he views as vital to safeguarding individual freedoms and judicial legitimacy.

item.title: Governo tem rombo de R$ 73,8 bi em março, o maior da história no mês
item.description: The central government recorded a primary deficit of R$ 73.8 billion in March 2026, the largest in the historical series for the month, exceeding analysts' projections. The deficit was driven by a sharp rise in expenditures, particularly precarious court payments and social security benefits, despite a 5.1% real increase in total revenue, boosted by IPI and IOF. The Lula administration had projected a primary surplus of R$ 3.5 billion for 2026, but the March result reveals a much larger shortfall, signaling fiscal strain.

item.title: O que se sabe sobre a investigação contra servidor que liberou bagagens sem raio-x em voo com Ciro e Motta
item.description: The Federal Police is investigating Receita Federal auditor Marco Antônio Canella for alleged prevarication and smuggling after he authorized the entry of five luggage items without X-ray screening on a private flight carrying Chamber President Hugo Motta and Senator Ciro Nogueira, returning from Sint Maarten on April 20, 2025. The case is before the Supreme Federal Court under Justice Alexandre de Moraes and also involves deputies Dr. Luizinho and Isnaldo Bulhões, as well as former councilman Victor Linhares, a target of Operation Carbono Oculto. The aircraft belongs to businessman Fernando Oliveira Lima (Fernandin OIG), owner of online betting platforms like Fortune Tiger, which was targeted by the Senate’s Bets CPI.

item.title: Brasil cria 228 mil vagas formais em março e supera projeções do mercado
item.description: Brazil created 228,208 formal jobs in March, exceeding market projections of 170,186 and marking the second-best March performance in recent series. The services sector led job creation, with São Paulo, Minas Gerais, and Rio de Janeiro showing the strongest gains, while agribusiness recorded a net loss. The average admission wage declined monthly but showed a real annual increase of 1.8%.

item.title: ‘Ninguém pode ser investigado a vida toda’, diz Messias sobre o Inquérito das Fake News
item.description: Union Attorney General Jorge Rodrigo Araújo Messias criticized the prolonged duration of the Fake News Inquiry, stating 'no one can be investigated for a lifetime' during his Senate hearing for STF nomination. He emphasized the need for principles such as natural judge, reasonable trial duration, and proportionality, arguing that criminal proceedings must serve justice, not vengeance.

item.title: Messias: “Zona cinzenta” pode levar AGU a tomar decisão que não é a melhor
item.description: The Attorney General of the Union and Lula's nominee to the STF, Jorge Messias, said disinformation remains a vague concept and that debates on freedom of expression often fall into a 'gray zone,' which may lead the AGU to make suboptimal decisions. He warned of the risks of flawed judgments in this ambiguous territory.

item.title: Senador Rogério Marinho declara que votou contra Messias para vaga ao STF
item.description: Senator Rogério Marinho (PL-RN) declared he voted against Jorge Messias' nomination to the Federal Supreme Court (STF), criticizing the Attorney General's Office (AGU) for creating a "Ministry of Truth" in its fight against disinformation, referencing George Orwell's "1984". He also denounced "endless investigations" at the STF, arguing they concentrate excessive power in a single minister, whom he labeled the "sheriff of Brazil", undermining judicial pluralism.

item.title: Senador questiona a indicação de Messias ao STF por supostamente ser jovem demais
item.description: Senator Esperidião Amin (PP-SC) criticized the nomination of Jorge Messias to the STF, claiming he is 'too young' and that the choice is driven by personal friendship and a desire for long tenure, which he deems unrepublican. In rebuttal, CCJ President Otto Alencar (PSD-BA) noted he had approved André Mendonça’s nomination — also relatively young — despite opposing Bolsonaro, emphasizing technical merit over age. Messias, at 46, could serve up to 29 years on the Court until mandatory retirement at 75.

item.title: Flávio usa sabatina de Messias para mirar Lula, STF e reanimar base bolsonarista
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro used Jorge Messias' STF sabatina as a political platform to attack Supreme Court decisions, defend January 8 defendants, and link the Lula government to corruption scandals like INSS and Banco Master. Analysts noted this was a strategic move to position himself as the main opposition leader and re-energize the Bolsonarist base, particularly by advocating amnesty and criticizing Minister Alexandre de Moraes. According to editor José Benedito da Silva, Flávio used the session to reinforce campaign messaging and engage radical segments of his electorate.

item.title: 'Ninguém pode ser investigado a vida toda', diz Messias ao ser questionado sobre inquérito das fake news
item.description: Union Attorney General Jorge Messias asserted that 'no one can be investigated for life' while defending the principle of reasonable duration in legal proceedings during his Senate CCJ hearing on the STF's fake news inquiry. Nominated by Lula for a STF ministerial seat, Messias requires 41 Senate votes for approval. The inquiry, ongoing since 2019, has been urged to end by the OAB over concerns of perpetual investigation, while PGR Paulo Gonet supports its continuation; Justice Alexandre de Moraes leads the case, and Justice Gilmar Mendes requested the inclusion of former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema due to a satirical video depicting STF justices as puppets.

item.title: Se aprovado no Senado, Messias mudará correlação de forças no STF
item.description: The potential approval of Jorge Messias by the Senate for the Supreme Federal Court could shift the Court’s internal balance of power, reinforcing the faction led by Edson Fachin, which advocates for a judicial ethics code and greater self-restraint. Although some justices, such as Gilmar Mendes and Alexandre de Moraes, have criticized congressional pressure on the Court, support for Messias is widespread among the judiciary. His confirmation hearing began on April 29, 2026, and he requires at least 41 Senate votes to fill the vacancy left by Luiz Roberto Barroso’s retirement.

item.title: Lula defenderá fim da escala 6 X 1 e novo Desenrola no 1º de Maio
item.description: President Lula will use the Workers' Day address to announce the reduction of the 6x1 workweek and the second phase of the Desenrola debt renegotiation program, targeting women and low-income workers. The measures aim to improve worker well-being, boost consumption in the second half of the year, and increase government popularity, with Desenrola 2.0 to be formally launched on May 4.

item.title: O que acontece se Jorge Messias for aprovado ou rejeitado em sabatina no Senado?
item.description: The Senate hearing of Jorge Messias determines his approval or rejection as a Supreme Court minister. If approved, it proceeds to a plenary vote requiring an absolute majority (41 senators). If rejected, President Lula must nominate another candidate, restarting the process.

item.title: Davi Alcolumbre libera voto contra Jorge Messias
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre has allowed his allies to vote against the nomination of Jorge Messias to the Supreme Federal Court, during the CCJ hearing. The move reflects ongoing political negotiations in Congress over the appointment of the new STF minister.

item.title: ‘Sabor agro’: Caiado ironiza falta de essência da nova geração do setor
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), pre-candidate for president, reaffirmed at the Agrishow in Ribeirão Preto (SP) that he will maintain his promise of broad, general, and unrestricted amnesty for those convicted in the January 8, 2023 attacks, including former President Bolsonaro. He justified his stance based on his political trajectory and self-identification as 'agro raiz', contrasting himself with a new generation he calls 'sabor agro' — superficial supporters of the agribusiness sector.

item.title: Ao vivo: Câmara instala a comissão sobre a 6 X 1
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies will install on Wednesday (April 29, 2026) at 2:00 PM a special committee to analyze constitutional amendment proposals aimed at ending the 6x1 work schedule and reducing the weekly workload. The committee will be chaired by Alencar Santana (PT-SP) with Léo Prates (Republicanos-BA) as rapporteur, reviewing PECs 221/2019 and 8/2025. Approval will require at least 3/5 of deputies in two rounds of voting in the plenary.

item.title: Ao vivo: STF julga ação sobre desoneração da folha
item.description: The STF is judging a case challenging the extension of payroll tax exemptions for 17 sectors until 2027 under Law 14.784/2023, assessing whether fiscal responsibility requirements were met. Simultaneously, the court is evaluating whether the Bolsonaro government's monitoring of journalists violated freedom of expression. Both cases carry major implications for Brazilian politics and the economy.

item.title: “8/1 foi um dos episódios mais tristes da história recente”, diz Messias a Flávio
item.description: The Attorney General of the Union and Lula’s nominee to the Supreme Federal Court, Jorge Messias, stated during a Senate CCJ hearing that January 8, 2023, was one of the saddest episodes in recent Brazilian history. He described the attacks on the seats of the Three Powers as a serious moment for democracy.

item.title: Com ministros e ex-ministros, tropa de choque governista vai ao Senado apoiar Messias em sabatina
item.description: Current Attorney General Jorge Messias attended a Senate hearing for his Supreme Court nomination, accompanied by Lula government ministers and former ministers including José Múcio, Silvio Costa Filho, Renan Filho, Wellington Dias, and Camilo Santana. The vote will be secret and tight: the government claims 25 secured votes, while 35 senators oppose and 21 are undecided, with 41 votes required for approval. João Campos, Lula-backed PSB pre-candidate for Pernambuco governor and polling at 46% in Quaest, also attended the hearing.

item.title: Tarcísio envia projeto para elevar salário mínimo paulista em 3,9%
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas sent a bill to Alesp raising São Paulo’s state minimum wage from R$1,804 to R$1,874 (3.9%), aligned with last year’s accumulated INPC. The increase aims to exceed the national minimum wage by 15% and covers over 70 professions, including caregivers for the elderly and disabled. The bill proceeds under urgency rules and could stall the legislative agenda if not approved within 45 days.

item.title: Messias nega a Flávio Bolsonaro que AGU tenha excluído manifestação ligada a Lulinha
item.description: The Attorney General of the Union, Jorge Messias, denied that the Advocacia Geral da União had excluded manifestations against unions linked to Lulinha, son of President Lula, during his tenure. The statement was made in response to allegations by Flávio Bolsonaro, reinforcing the AGU’s stance of neutrality in politically sensitive matters.

item.title: Governistas trabalham até o fim por apoio de Alcolumbre a Messias no STF
item.description: Government allies are working until the end to secure the support of Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP) for Lula's nominee Jorge Messias to the Supreme Federal Court, while his confirmation hearing proceeds in the Senate's Constitution and Justice Committee. The effort reflects the government's attempt to guarantee a favorable vote amid potential resistance from its own base.

item.title: TJDFT envia a Moraes certidão de antecedentes criminais de Eduardo
item.description: The Federal District's Court of Justice sent to Minister Alexandre de Moraes of the STF the criminal record certificate of former deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro, containing a single 2019 case for alleged insult and threat, already archived. The submission complies with a judicial order within an action investigating alleged procedural coercion linked to articulations with the U.S. government.
